chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Al-Husayn ibn Usman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Bakr Al-Hazramy, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who prays and upon him is his dye. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not pray while it is upon him, but he should remove it when he intends to pray.' I said, 'If his henna and his cloth are clean?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He cannot pray while it is upon him; and the woman as well, she cannot pray and upon her is her dye.'

key_terms.خِضَابُهُ: dye or henna applied to the body

ai.seo_question: Does a person need to remove henna or dye from their body or clothes before performing prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the presence of henna or dye on the body or clothing invalidates the prayer unless removed, emphasizing that mere cleanliness of the dye is insufficient for validity. This ruling applies equally to men and women, highlighting the importance of removing physical impediments to the proper performance of *salat*. The narration underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the integrity of the prayer requires the removal of such substances, reflecting a strict adherence to ritual purity and completeness in worship.
